prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

New part:
S784: Emergency access may be granted to the Emergency Response Coordinator, Airport Duty Manager, or System Support Engineer when life safety, airport continuity, or critical system recovery requires immediate action.
S785: Use of emergency access shall generate prominent audit events and shall require post-event review by the Data Governance Steward and the responsible operational authority.
S786: During Contingency Fallback State, access control shall continue to enforce role separation even when some integrations are unavailable and manual coordination becomes necessary.
S787: When normal connectivity is restored, the Regional Flow Platform shall reconcile contingency actions with the Collaborative Decision Log so that accountability is preserved across the full incident timeline.
S788: After connectivity is restored, audit processing shall treat reconciled contingency actions as part of the same operational record as actions taken during Normal Operations.
S789: The Regional Flow Platform shall record slot compliance events in the Audit Event Ledger using the operating date, flight identifier, airport, runway direction, and applicable regulation reference.
S790: Each compliance assessment shall compare the Calculated Takeoff Time, the Target Off Block Time, actual off-block time, and actual takeoff time against the tolerance defined in the Business Rules Registry.
S791: The Slot Compliance State shall indicate whether a flight was compliant, early, late, exempted, substituted, cancelled, or pending review at the end of the traffic period.
S792: The Audit Event Ledger shall preserve the time source applied by the Time Synchronization Service so that later review can distinguish operational delay from data latency.
S793: User decisions entered through the Airport CDM Portal shall be linked to the authenticated role provided by the Identity Access Service.
S794: The Collaborative Decision Log shall retain the stated reason, decision time, affected flight, and visible operational context for each material change to a slot or sequence.
S795: The Airline Operations Coordinator uses the permission email to justify an approved slot substitution during post-operations review.
S796: Substitution records shall show the original flight, replacement flight, assigned Calculated Takeoff Time, acceptance status, and any subsequent cancellation or reversion.
S797: When an Aircraft Operator Representative proposes a substitution, the audit trail shall capture whether the change preserved the constraints of the active Ground Delay Program.
S798: The Slot Coordinator shall review substitution activity after operations to confirm that priority rules were applied consistently across participating operators.
S799: Late operational changes shall be distinguished from planned updates by comparing the change timestamp with the freeze horizon held in the Business Rules Registry.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
